data_origin: GitHub Actions hosted CI; not physical user-machine submissions

scope.baseline: Frozen fast.8 PackedRealDiskFFT._tile reconstruction method in the current implementation
scope.candidate: Current packed-real reconstruction method at source_commit
scope.shared: FFTW binary, native library, input, output grid, resource limits, FFT core, preprocessing and aggregation are identical within each comparison.
scope.timing: Fresh complete PSD+NSD calls, including planning, preprocessing, diagnostics and cleanup. Signal generation/hashing, imports, library loading and class selection are outside each timer.
scope.phase_units: Wall-clock seconds measured with time.perf_counter; cpu_s is process CPU time for the complete call.
scope.order: Three pairs per configuration, alternating baseline/candidate, candidate/baseline, baseline/candidate.
limits: N=1,000,000 with generated white noise and 577/1,154 actual output points; these files fit in RAM.
This is a comparison of two packed-real reconstructions, not full-complex versus packed-real.
Small CI timings do not establish out-of-RAM storage performance, billion-sample performance, or physical user-device performance.
Runner variance and cache state remain; ranges are provided and no speed threshold is a correctness gate.
The archived files contain all timing and comparison records, not raw spectra; complete output bytes were compared by the source-verified harness during execution.

interpretation: The complete-call FFTW medians are lower for the new packed reconstruction in all eight platform/point-count configurations; individual ranges still matter.
Matched/Hybrid savings are smaller because other phases dominate; macOS at 1,154 points has a higher candidate median in this cohort.
Do not rank CPUs from absolute times across different runners or multiply these gains by earlier full-versus-packed gains.
Defaults are not selected by these timing samples; correctness and successful platform execution are the CI gates.

windows_runtime_confirmation.qualification: This is an actual Windows GitHub Actions run with the private bootstrap; it is not a physical user-machine submission or a full native Windows pytest matrix.

native_ci_gate.name: Native tests and wheel
native_ci_gate.scope: Separate package/numerical CI gate; native benchmark timings are not used to claim a fast.8-to-fast.9 gain.
native_ci_gate.test_count_note: Per-job and per-suite counts; FFTW and disk subsets overlap the full optimized suite and repeated platform jobs are not summed as unique tests.
